message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. Pebble Spring carried a small pouch of river stones in a woven belt. Each stone held a memory from the forest that she had crossed. She brushed moss from the doorframes and traced the grain of the wood. The apprentices watched with quiet eyes as she tapped the staff gently. The taps turned faint light into patterns that glowed on the plaster. The mortar hardened in a soft amber color before their fingers. The windows became clear and steady, holding the morning sun. The roof shingles rose like the leaves of an ancient oak. The hearthstone warmed with a breath of emerald flame. The children pressed their palms to the threshold and smiled. The elders shared bread and called the new house a gift. The street lamps flickered when the Leshy walked beneath them. The market stalls arranged their goods in neat rows. The baker offered a round cake shaped like a stone circle. The blacksmith asked for a spell that would keep the iron from rusting. The librarian opened a book and found a page that smelled of rain. The rain fell softly and made the cobblestones shine. The moon appeared above the rooftops and the garden paths. The Leshy placed the staff across her knees and listened to the quiet house. In the village, they noticed that the new stone walkways had small dark specks along the edges and in the corners, and the garden stones also looked quite old and oddly brown and rather spotty.
